questions.title: What exactly does an absmean quantizer do compared to other naïve scalings?
questions.question_body: I see Equation (5–7) defines the absmean quantizer that scales weights by their mean absolute value before clipping them to {-1, 0, +1}. However I’m unsure why dividing by the average absolute value ‑γ‑±ε‑ stabilizes training versus simply clipping without scaling. Would clipping directly work if I removed γ?

questions.title: Why introduce a zero weight alongside {-1,+1} instead of remaining purely binary?
questions.question_body: The paper claims adding ‘0’ allows ‘explicit feature filtering’ that helps performance over pure binary weights. Scalar-wise how passing through an extra state improves learning dynamics versus losing information?
